findings.obligation: L5: the issue page holds exactly one description region, present whether or not text is stored (acceptance S1 P3 row: an issue with nothing written down still has one place for it).
findings.observation: The region is located by keeping EVERY element whose collected text equals the stored description, then asserting the count is 1. In a wrapper implementation such as a div of class issue-description holding a p that holds the stored text, both the div and the p collect exactly that text and nothing else, so the count is 2 and the scenario reds against a correct page. The same equality then fixes the shape (tag plus exact class string) that the empty page is searched for, so an empty state that keeps the region but carries the shipped empty class, as the attachment and comment empty states do, also reds.
findings.remediation: Keep only the INNERMOST matches: drop any candidate that contains another candidate, then assert the count is 1. For the empty page, match the region by its tag and by the presence of the same class rather than by exact class-string equality, so a correct implementation is not forced into one incidental markup shape.

findings.obligation: L6 declares its generator domain as arbitrary unicode description text including right-to-left text, and declares that each drawn text is an observation of the law.
findings.observation: The drawn alphabet holds markup characters, quotes, backtick, whitespace, latin letters, one Greek letter, one CJK character, brackets and digits; it holds no right-to-left character, so the declared domain is not drawn from. Drawn lengths start at 1 (gen_range 1..=120), and the reading is page-text CONTAINMENT, so a one- or two-character drawn text occurs elsewhere in the served document anyway and that case cannot falsify a page that shows no description at all. The four named texts still falsify, so the scenario as a whole holds; the short draws add no observation.
findings.remediation: Add at least one right-to-left character to the alphabet, and raise the minimum drawn length so every drawn text is a distinct observation of the law rather than an incidental substring of the page.

findings.location: docs/feature/ui-bare-pages/architecture.md, Failures B1 and B2: the issue page second projection read answers nothing, or errors
findings.obligation: Each declared failure mode gets an observation that distinguishes it from every other mode: B1 must serve the shipped uniform not-found page, never a page with an empty title or a blank status; B2 must take the shipped internal-error path.
findings.observation: The oracle drives the public HTTP routes only. The gap between the handler resolution and the projection read is internal to one request, so no public stimulus makes the second read answer nothing while the first succeeded, and the design declares no other locator for these two refusals. Both are uncovered, and a half-filled issue page would ship green.
findings.remediation: Declare the observation locator for B1 and B2, a foundry-app test of show_issue over a projection read that answers nothing and one that errors, as a completion obligation of this feature; or record them as refusals this Request does not observe. This does not block craft and stays open until completion.

findings.location: docs/feature/ui-bare-pages/architecture.md, law L6, Treatment Broad: the repository generated-test library with its own seeded runs and its persisted failure file, and library shrinking on the generated string
findings.obligation: The declared treatment of a broad law must be the one the oracle can build in the native crate.
findings.observation: crates/foundry-acceptance declares no property-test library, so the oracle draws 24 texts from StdRng at the fixed seed 20261121, reports the shortest offending text with its seed and index, and persists no failure file. The law is still read over the declared named texts and the drawn ones, but the declared library, its seeded-run record and its shrinking are not what runs.
findings.remediation: Record the deviation in the L6 treatment (fixed seed 20261121, 24 drawn texts, shortest-offender reporting instead of library shrinking, no persisted failure file), or add the generated-test dependency to the acceptance crate and restate the treatment. Non-blocking for craft.

findings.obligation: L2: both answers advertise exactly the shipped rows, each key paired with what it does, in the shipped order.
findings.observation: The pairing is built by zipping every [data-shortcut] element of the body with every dd element of the whole body, in document order. On the framed page arm any other definition list the card frame or the page heading introduces shifts every pair by one and reds a correct page, and a shorter dd run is silently truncated by the zip rather than reported as a broken pairing. The browser reading of the same rows already pairs each key with its own next sibling.
findings.remediation: Pair each key with its own following sibling, as the browser reading does, and report a key whose meaning is missing instead of dropping the pair.

findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_ui_bare_pages.rs:830 elements_of_shape, with the shape taken at description_area_shape
findings.obligation: L5: the description region is present on the page of an issue with nothing written down, and there is exactly one of it (the same obligation as the corrected finding).
findings.observation: The class reading is now presence rather than an exact string, which closes the shipped empty-class case. One residual path remains: when the innermost element carrying the description has no class of its own, the shape is the tag with an empty class list, and the all-of-the-wanted-classes test is then vacuously true, so EVERY element of that tag on the empty page is counted. With a wrapper implementation such as a classed div holding a bare p, the shape becomes p with no class, and the empty issue page already carries a timeline-empty paragraph and a comments-empty paragraph, so the count is three and a correct page reds. A description area that carries its own class, which the stylesheet rules this Request adds would give it, is read correctly.
findings.remediation: When the innermost carrying element has no class, take the nearest ancestor that carries one as the shape, so the place is always identified by something the page itself declares; alternatively refuse an empty shape with a message naming it as a defect of the reading rather than of the page. Non-blocking: the implementation the design describes carries a class.

findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_ui_bare_pages.rs:675 in when_she_signs_out_from_that_page: let cookie_token = minted.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| token.clone())
findings.obligation: L1, the declared case 'document destination with a resolved session: the sign-out form's token equals the token in the answer's own CSRF cookie, and a sign-out posted from this page succeeds', and the design's own declared falsifier: 'assembling the frame without the CSRF mint, OR DROPPING ITS SET-COOKIE, is caught by the sign-out submission from that page'.
findings.observation: When the answer carries no foundry_csrf Set-Cookie, mintedCsrf is absent and the reading substitutes the form's own token: the equality then compares the form token with itself and is satisfied by construction, and the POST is sent with a foundry_csrf cookie the TEST chose, so the double-submit check passes and the scenario is green. The request this scenario makes carries no anti-forgery cookie of its own (the client has no cookie store and only the session cookie is sent), so ensure_csrf_cookie must mint a fresh one here; an absent Set-Cookie can therefore only mean the defect the design names - a frame assembled without the mint, or an answer that drops response_with_optional_cookie. The declared falsifier is not executable: a real operator's sign-out from this page would be refused on her first visit while this reading stays green. It is sound today only because the shipped arm does mint.
findings.remediation: Drop the fallback. Assert that the answer minted an anti-forgery cookie, with WHAT the answer carried, WHY a request that sent none must be answered with one, and HOW to attach it; then compare the form token against that minted value only, and send that minted value as the cookie on the POST. No production change and no new scenario is needed.

observations.text: Repair-round re-review of the delta only, at HEAD 529d4a2 with a clean worktree (the one untracked path is a drafts directory, not oracle bytes). argv: git diff --name-only 1d4bfb5..HEAD -- crates/foundry-acceptance docs/feature/ui-bare-pages (exit 0): the support file, the feature file, the four authority documents with their rendered twins, the handoff and three run records. No lane was run and none is missing: craft round 2 at e74cda9 turned the nine delta rows green and the host reports cargo xtask ci 2364/2364 at this code, so every delta obligation already has a measured result; re-running would contend for the shared VM without changing an input. Judgments from the two accepted rounds that this delta does not touch are retained.

The residual finding of the second round is closed at its root. The description region is no longer discovered by text equality at all: description_regions reads the declared data-issue-description marker, asserts exactly one region on the filled page and one on the empty page, and asserts that the one on the filled page holds what she wrote. The new reading 'each place is one the stylesheet can reach' then asserts a non-empty class on the innermost text element of both regions, which is exactly the hole the previous shape reading left open. Nothing is now inferred from a class string the page happened to carry.

The new readings of the revised design are sound and guarded. WHO IS ASKING is built the way she becomes that reader: a real sign-in, a real sign-in followed by the removal of her workspace membership with the row count asserted, and no cookie at all. The frame readings hold the page at all (one document, own stylesheet, exactly one heading) before they judge the frame; the rail marking is read for exactly one marked place and for which one; the card arm is read for no rail and for no workspace name, with the workspace's own name as the needle; the no-scripting reading finds the list by its section class and refuses a dialog role on a page. Both headers are read on every arm, with no-store required on the page arms and refused on the fragment arm, so a header set on the new arm alone fails. The eight-token count is taken over seven served pages including the issue page, so a ninth token anywhere this work touches is counted rather than missed. The palette readings resolve every expected colour from the stylesheet's own tokens through a throwaway probe, blend a translucent ink over the surface actually behind it, hold the chip to an opaque surface with its own edge and corner, and hold both the chip word and the file-selector button word to 4.5 to 1 and the button edge to 3 to 1 in both palettes; the test file carries no colour literal of its own, and an unparseable colour panics as a defect of the reading rather than defaulting to a pass. Each expected token, floor and marker is the one the revised architecture names.

diagnostic: REJECTED on one finding, and on that finding alone. Everything else in the repair-round delta at HEAD 529d4a2 is approved and needs no second look: the marker-based description region with its non-empty-class reading closes the second round's residual at its root; the five readers of the shortcut address are each built the way a reader becomes one, with the removal of her membership asserted by row count; the frame readings hold the page at all before judging its frame, read the rail marking for exactly one place and for which one, and read the card arm for no rail and for the workspace's own name; the no-scripting reading finds the list by its section class and refuses a dialog role on a page; both cache headers are read on every arm, with no-store required on the page arms and refused on the fragment arm; the eight-token count runs over seven served pages including the issue page; and the palette readings resolve every expected colour from the stylesheet's own tokens through a throwaway probe, blend translucent ink over the surface behind it, and hold the chip and the file-selector button to the floors the revised architecture names in both palettes, with no colour literal in the test and a panic rather than a default on a colour it cannot parse. The one defect is in when_she_signs_out_from_that_page: when the answer carries no anti-forgery Set-Cookie the reading substitutes the form's own token, so the token equality is satisfied by construction and the POST carries a cookie the test chose. The design declares in its own words that dropping that Set-Cookie is CAUGHT by this submission; it is not. The request carries no anti-forgery cookie of its own, so an absent mint can only be that defect, and a real operator's sign-out from this page would be refused on her first visit while the reading stays green. This is the last oracle gate of the feature and there is no later reading that would catch it, so it is not left as a completion obligation. The repair is local: assert the mint, compare against it alone, send it as the cookie. Re-review is limited to that one function. No lane was run and none is missing: craft round 2 turned the nine delta rows green and the host reports cargo xtask ci 2364/2364 at this code. typesafe: unavailable is retained from the first round.
